entities.name: Khabekhnet
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Khabekhnet, an Ancient Egyptian artisan, stands as a pivotal figure for understanding the daily lives, religious convictions, and social structures of the New Kingdom's working class. Living in the meticulously documented village of Deir el-Medina on the west bank of the Nile, opposite Thebes, during the extensive reign of Ramesses II (c. 1279–1213 BCE), Khabekhnet's well-preserved tomb, TT2, offers historians and archaeologists an unparalleled window into the lives of the necropolis workers responsible for constructing and decorating the royal tombs in the Valley of the Kings and Queens. His existence underscores the specialized labor and community organization that underpinned the monumental funerary architecture of the era.

Khabekhnet served as a 'Servant in the Place of Truth,' a title designating the elite artisans who crafted the pharaohs' eternal resting places. He was the son of the revered foreman Sennedjem and Iyneferti, inheriting a position within a prominent family of skilled craftsmen. His personal life, extensively detailed through tomb inscriptions and papyri, reveals he was married to Sahti and likely also to a woman named Isis, reflecting the complex familial and social networks within Deir el-Medina. His work, alongside his peers, contributed to the visual and theological narrative of the pharaonic afterlife, a testament to the highly developed artistic and religious traditions of the 19th Dynasty.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Khabekhnet's well-preserved tomb provides an exceptionally detailed and intimate look into the daily life, family structure, and religious beliefs of a non-royal artisan community in New Kingdom Egypt, offering insights rarely available for common individuals of this era.
